Cat Café

Every number is a cat, and the nine cats sit around a wheel in order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, black and white.

House rule: cats that sit next to each other on the wheel are territorial. They won’t share a side, up, down, left or right. White and red are neighbors too, since the wheel wraps around. Diagonals are fine.

The usual sudoku rules still apply. Fill a box correctly and its cats curl up for a nap.

Mahjong

You can only place numbers you hold. Your hand has up to five tiles: tap a tile, then a cell, or a cell, then a tile. Each correct placement draws a new tile.

Every tile has somewhere to go. You never hold more of a number than the board has open spots for, so late in the game your hand shrinks.

Correct tile+10
Finish a row, column or box (each)+50
Pung: three of the same number in a row+100
Chow: three numbers in sequence, like 4 5 6+60
Redraw the selected tile−10
Wrong tile (counts as a mistake)−20

Melds count consecutive correct placements, in any cells. A wrong tile breaks the streak and stays in your hand. Undo restores your score and hand, but it can’t reroll a draw.

Mountain Goat

Your goat starts in the valley at the bottom of the board. It can only reach the eight cells around it, so you solve the puzzle along a trail instead of wherever is easiest.

ClimbFill a highlighted cell next to your goat. A correct number moves the goat onto it.
LeapA number in any other cell is a leap and costs a bale of hay. Out of hay, the goat still leaps but it counts as a rescue.
HayYou start with a few bales. Every box you finish earns another.
SnortA wrong number is never written. The goat snorts, stays put and it counts as a mistake.
HintFills a cell next to the goat, or gives it a free lift when it is boxed in.

Plan your route: a cell you can solve now may be across the board. Notes work anywhere and cost nothing. Finish without a rescue to be sure-footed.

Melody

Every number is a note. 1 is the lowest and 9 the highest, climbing a pentatonic scale over two octaves, so any order of notes sounds musical.

PlaceA correct number plays its note. A wrong one sounds sour, so your ear can catch mistakes too.
CompleteFinishing a row, column or box plays it back as a phrase, cell by cell.
PlayPlays the board as it stands, row by row. Empty cells are rests.
SongSolve the puzzle and the grid becomes a song: nine bars, one per row, over a bass line.

Everything else is classic sudoku. Turn sound on to play.

Reverse

Reverse starts from a finished grid and runs sudoku backward. Bold numbers are clues still on the board. Faded numbers have been removed. Some are already gone when you start.

Your goal is to remove as many clues as you can while the puzzle still has only one solution. Fewer clues makes a harder puzzle, and a better score.

RemoveTap a bold number. If the puzzle still has one solution, it fades.
BlockedIf removing it would allow a second solution, it stays and counts as a mistake. The empty cells that could change flash red with the numbers they could become.
Put backTap a faded number to restore it. This is always allowed.
Hint ModePuts a padlock on clues that can’t be removed right now and shows how many still can.
HintMakes one removable clue glow.
ParEasy 28 · Medium 26 · Hard 25 · Expert 23 clues.

Order matters: each removal can lock other clues in place, so careful choices can finish several clues lower than quick ones. A finished puzzle can be missing at most one number entirely, so the last copy of a number is often locked.

The game ends by itself when nothing more can be removed. Tap Finish to stop early.

Dungeon

Each floor is a puzzle. Clear it to reach the shop, then descend. Every two floors you go deeper and the puzzles get harder: Surface, Smoothrock, Dirt, Rock, then Lava.

Hearts. You start with five. A wrong number costs a heart and is never written. At zero hearts the run ends.

Coins. Every box you complete drops 3 coins, and clearing a floor pays 5 plus 2 per floor number. In the shop, a healing potion costs 8 (up to 7 hearts), a hint scroll 5 and a peek scroll 6.

Peek. Tap Peek, then any cell. That box’s answers show faintly for 3 seconds.

Traps start on floor 3:

FogHides the corner boxes. Correct numbers and Peek light the way.
ClockWhen it runs out you lose a heart and get 90 more seconds.
CurseA cell’s notes scramble every 12 seconds until you place its number. Lifting it pays 2 coins.

Your run saves as you play. Tapping New Game twice abandons it.
